claims.text: Composition optimization can introduce a nanocrystalline structure into a refractory high-entropy alloy.
A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy will have 25% higher yield strength than a conventional coarse-grained refractory high-entropy alloy.
The predicted yield-strength improvement will occur at temperatures above 800°C.
The predicted yield-strength improvement will persist under irradiation.
The nanocrystalline structure increases the contribution of grain boundaries to strengthening.
Grain-boundary strengthening causes the predicted increase in yield strength.
The hypothesis is intended to hold only at irradiation doses below 10 dpa.
The magnitude of the yield-strength improvement may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Defect accumulation and microstructural evolution may affect irradiation stability.
The proposed comparison will test nanocrystalline and coarse-grained alloys after irradiation to 10 dpa at 800°C.
The hypothesis will be deemed falsified if the nanocrystalline alloy's yield strength is less than 15% higher than that of the conventional alloy.

contradictions.description: The claimed temperature domain is above 800°C, whereas the experiment is conducted at exactly 800°C and therefore does not directly test the stated domain.
The stated boundary is below 10 dpa, but the experiment uses exactly 10 dpa.

The prediction specifies a 25% improvement, but the falsification threshold is only 15%; an outcome between 15% and 25% would fail the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
